L01.note: 16 is the hub: 4^2 = 16 and 16 - 4 = 12; 49 is the stray square.

L03.note: 12 is the hub: 7 and 17 sit symmetrically at 12 +/- 5, and 4 = 12/3.

L05.note: 15 = 9 + 6 (sum hub); 0 reads as the no-solution trap.

L06.note: 156 = 12*13 shares a factor with both 168 = 12*14 and 234 = 18*13; 174 is the loner.

L07.note: 2.5 is the lone non-integer among 1, 6, 9; the integers look like equation constants.

L08.note: no signal (-8/-32 form a x4 pair, -12/-18 a x1.5 pair; cannot break the tie).

L09.note: 49 and 51 flank 50 at +/-1; 50 is the hub with 45 the off-by-5 distractor.

L10.note: -17 is the weak hub: -14 = -17 + 3 and -26 = -17 - 9 (3 and 3^2); -4 is the stray.

L11.note: 49.8 is the lone computed decimal; 5, 9, 20 look like constants lifted from the model.

L13.note: 11 and -53 sit symmetrically at -21 +/- 32; -21 is the hub.

L14.note: 91.7% = 11/12 exactly, the only designed-looking fraction; 83.9% is the cluster outlier.

L15.note: 24 is the hub: 24 = 4*6, 29 = 24 + 5, and 10 = 6 + 4 reuses the same parts.

L17.note: The +/-6 sign pair marks the key; -6 is the sign-kept version, 6 the dropped-sign trap.

L21.note: no signal; 36 taken only as the designed-looking square.

L22.note: 17/19 adjacent-prime pair suggests the key is one of them, but no way to choose; 17 arbitrary.

L23.note: no signal; 10 is the magnitude outlier, 0 the no-solution trap, -2 arbitrary between the rest.

L24.note: 1.331 = 1.1^3, so 33.1% per 3 years is 10% per year and 2000(1.1)^5 is the value the others are built around.

L25.note: 2, 4, 16 form a 2^x chain; 4 is the middle exponent-style value (2^4 = 16, 4 = 2^2).

L26.note: 23 is the hub: 7 = 23 - 16 and 55 = 23 + 32, with 25 the off-by-2 neighbour.

L27.note: 33, 41, 51, 63 are consecutive outputs of one quadratic (differences 8, 10, 12), so all four are equally designed; 51 arbitrary.
